Phase 2 of the automation base, UniFi read-only, and device passwords
encrypted at rest. Coming from 4.16.0 it's a plain `helm upgrade`, but your
device passwords get encrypted on the first start, and from then on the key is
part of your data. Read "Upgrading from 4.16.0" below before you touch a
running plant.

The full notes are in the README:
What changed in 4.17.0.

## In short

- **The automation base, phase 2.** Helpers (the values the plant's people
  own, refused and never clamped), the logbook (one timeline of state changes,
  writes, alarms, runs and config), condition, wait and stop steps and
  `forSec` on a state trigger, scripts (write the CIP cycle once, run it from
  anywhere), recipes (every setpoint for a grade goes out together or none do,
  read back from the device) and blueprints (a rule written once, filled in per
  pump, pinned to its version until somebody reviews the upgrade). MCP goes
  from 16 tools to 25.
- **UniFi Network, read-only.** Switches, ports, PoE, WAN and clients as tags,
  one login per console, the certificate pinned. A quiet PLC's drawer says
  which switch port it's on and whether the link is up, and a stranger on a
  network marked OT raises an alarm. Proven read-only on real consoles.
  **Not proven yet:** a real cable pull on a watched device and a phone joining
  a network marked OT. Those two alarms are proven in the lab and nowhere else
  until somebody does both at the rack.
- **Device passwords are encrypted** in the database and in backups, with a
  key the chart generates into `<release>-secret-key` and keeps.
- **Fixes a 4.16.0 plant can trip over:** an Edge Relay from the chart or the
  Quadlet unit ignored every config push, and one with persistence off didn't
  boot; a hand edit in the rule editor reset the rule's run budget; the command
  prompt's verdict could move Set out from under the click; a late update could
  put the Entities screen back in time; a rule that never ran said it ran
  739887 days ago; App Store deploys carried no tenant.

### API changes

- A time that hasn't happened is left out, not sent as `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`:
  `lastRun`, `lastPoll`, `lastGood`, `clearedAt`, `ackedAt`, `shelvedUntil`,
  `raisedAt` and the rest, on the live feed too.
- New routes: `/api/helpers`, `/api/logbook`, `/api/scripts`, `/api/recipes`,
  `/api/blueprints`, `POST /api/automations/{id}/blueprint-upgrade`,
  `/api/devices/{id}/network`, `/api/unifi/{id}/...` and
  `DELETE /api/fleet/{id}/config`. All in docs/API.md.
- New permissions, and the operator role has them: `helpers.write`,
  `scripts.run`, `recipes.apply`, `blueprints.apply`. Writing scripts, recipes
  and blueprints is admin.
- Tags carry `deviceClass`; rules carry `blueprintId`, `blueprintVersion` and
  `blueprintInputs`.

### Upgrading from 4.16.0

- `helm upgrade <release> hotloop/hotloop --version 4.17.0
  --reset-then-reuse-values`. Not `--reuse-values`, which drops the new
  defaults and fails to render. Selectors and volume claims are unchanged; the
  only new object is the key's Secret.
- Migrations 0009 to 0015 run on start (helpers, logbook, scripts, tag device
  class, recipes, blueprints, UniFi). All additive. `pg_dump` first.
- `HOTLOOP_SECRET_KEY_FILE`: the chart generates the key on this upgrade, and
  the Gateway encrypts every stored device password at that start. Without the
  key afterwards, those devices stay down with an error naming the key. A backup
  taken after the upgrade restores only with that key, or with
  `--restore-keep-unreadable-credentials`, which leaves those devices down until
  somebody enters the passwords again. Back the Secret up away from your
  backups. Going back to 4.16.0 means restoring your pre-upgrade dump.
- Rendering the chart with `helm template` instead of installing it? Bring your
  own key in `secretKey.existingSecret`, or every render makes a new one.
- Edge Relay: a pushed device file lives at `/data/pushed-devices.json` and
  wins over the chart's `devices` while it exists; `DELETE
  /api/fleet/{id}/config` clears it. A push that failed on 4.16.0 is still
  retained on the broker and lands at the first 4.17.0 boot. Quadlet users take
  the new unit. `persistence.enabled=false` boots now and loses the forward
  queue, any pushed file and the OPC UA certificate every time the pod is
  replaced.
